description: All-weather interceptor displayed at the locality named „Кај Авионите“ beside Bitola city park; the OpenStreetMap surveyor recorded the tactical number 14078 and the operator as the Air Force of the SFRY in Macedonian; Yugoslav F-86Ds carried 14xxx numbers so the serial block is internally consistent; not confirmed against a second source
aliases: F86; F-86D; Sabre; Sabre Dog; F86D

description: Day fighter Sabre displayed beside the F-86D at Bitola; tactical number 11056 and the SFRY Air Force operator recorded by the OpenStreetMap surveyor; Yugoslav day-fighter Sabres — Canadair CL-13 Mk.4 airframes as well as North American F-86Es — carried 11xxx numbers; whether this airframe is a genuine North American F-86E or a Canadair-built Sabre Mk.4 is NOT established and the surveyor's F-86E label may be the local designation rather than the build standard
aliases: F86; F-86E; Sabre; CL-13; Sabre Mk4; F86E; CL13
